headline: High-risk shared-workspace pair: Cline can overwrite Chatwoot outputs and both can leak sensitive customer data through broad network egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot can surface customer messages and reports, while Cline can read workspace files, use MCP, and run browsers. If Chatwoot content is copied into files or MCP-fed prompts, Cline may treat attacker-controlled text as instructions. The pathway is plausible but not default between these two without an explicit bridge.
conditions: IF Chatwoot output is copied into a workspace file that Cline reads
IF an MCP server forwards Chatwoot content into Cline prompts
IF a support message contains instruction-like text and Cline is asked to summarize it
mitigations: Keep Chatwoot exports out of Cline workspaces
Disable MCP servers that ingest support content
Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from pasted text
Review any file Cline reads from Chatwoot before execution
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between support content and agent prompts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, and has broad network egress. Cline reads and writes workspace files and also has broad network egress. If the shared workspace contains customer records, either agent can move them off-box; Cline’s file access makes leakage especially direct.
conditions: IF customer data is stored in a workspace file accessible to Cline
IF Chatwoot exports reports or messages into files that Cline can read
IF either agent is configured to send file contents to a remote model provider
mitigations: Keep customer data outside shared workspaces
Restrict Cline to a scrubbed sandbox workspace
Disable network egress for nonessential Chatwoot integrations
Redact customer identifiers before any file handoff
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory access controls and DLP

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and a filesystem-based shared_state_with_other_instances; Chatwoot can also operate on reports and integrations that may produce files. In a shared workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide and corrupt state. The conflict is default-dangerous for Cline and plausible for the pair.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same workspace directory
IF Cline modifies git state while Chatwoot-generated artifacts are present
IF either agent writes to the same report or export file
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git worktrees or branches per agent
Avoid letting Chatwoot export into the coding workspace
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can generate customer-facing reports and messages, and Cline can act on files and browser state. If Cline consumes Chatwoot output as authoritative without verification, mistakes can cascade into incorrect edits or actions. The pair does not prove automatic action chaining, so medium is the higher justified severity.
conditions: IF Cline is instructed to act on Chatwoot-generated summaries without human review
IF Chatwoot output is pasted into Cline as ground truth
IF Cline uses browser or shell actions based on unverified support text
mitigations: Require human review before any action based on Chatwoot output
Ask Cline to cite source files before acting
Use a checklist to verify customer-facing facts
Limit Cline to drafting, not executing, from Chatwoot inputs
requires-engineering: add validation gates between support output and actions

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, and orders, while Cline handles workspace files and model-provider API keys. If customer data is placed into Cline’s workspace or prompts, it can flow to a third-party model provider under different retention and residency terms. The profiles do not prove a residency mismatch, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF customer data is entered into Cline prompts or workspace files
IF the model provider retains prompts differently than Chatwoot retains support records
IF the deployment handles regulated customer data
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Cline prompts
Use a provider with compatible retention terms
Review Chatwoot and model-provider retention settings
Mask personal data before transfer
requires-engineering: formalize a data-processing agreement and residency controls
